content: Aprepitant is a medication used in combination with other drugs to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy. It is not effective for treating nausea or vomiting that has already started. The medication works by inhibiting the substance P/neurokinin 1 (NK1) receptors in the brain, which are involved in the vomiting reflex. Aprepitant has minimal or no affinity for serotonin (5-HT3), dopamine, or corticosteroid receptors. In animal and human studies, it has been shown to enhance the antiemetic effects of ondansetron (a 5-HT3 receptor antagonist) and dexamethasone (a corticosteroid), effectively reducing both acute and delayed phases of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. How to Use: Aprepitant is taken orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. The first dose is typically taken one hour before the start of chemotherapy. For the next two days, it is taken once daily, one hour before treatment if chemotherapy is administered on those days. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, age, and response to treatment. For children, the dosage is also based on weight. It is important to follow your doctor’s instructions regarding the timing, duration, and strength of each dose. Side Effects: Common side effects may include tiredness or hiccups. Serious allergic reactions are rare but can occur. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. Contact your doctor for medical advice if you experience any unusual symptoms. Precautions: Before taking aprepitant, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, fosaprepitant, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, aprepitant should only be used when clearly needed, as there is insufficient data on its safety in pregnant women. Avoid the intravenous emulsion form of aprepitant during pregnancy due to its alcohol content. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk, so a decision should be made to discontinue nursing or the drug, considering its importance to the mother. Drug Interactions: Aprepitant can interact with other medications, potentially altering their effectiveness or increasing the risk of side effects. Examples of interacting drugs include azole antifungals (e.g., itraconazole, ketoconazole), macrolide antibiotics (e.g., clarithromycin, erythromycin), HIV protease inhibitors (e.g., nelfinavir), rifamycins (e.g., rifampin), and St. John’s Wort. Aprepitant may also affect the metabolism of warfarin, hormonal contraceptives, and other medications. Women using hormonal contraceptives should use an effective alternative or backup non-hormonal method (e.g., condoms or spermicides) during treatment and for one month after the last dose. Storage: Store capsules at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. The liquid form should be refrigerated and discarded after 72 hours if unused. Do not freeze the liquid. When ready to use, the liquid may be stored at room temperature for up to three hours. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Overdose: In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention. In the U.S., call 911 for severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, or contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Additional Information: Aprepitant is highly protein-bound (>95%) and has a bioavailability of 60-65% when taken orally. It crosses the blood-brain barrier and is metabolized primarily by the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4, with minor contributions from CYP1A2 and CYP2C19. It inhibits CYP3A4 and induces CYP2C9. The half-life of aprepitant is approximately 9-13 hours, and it is excreted via urine (57%) and feces (45%). It is not dialyzable. Always inspect the vial for particulate matter or discoloration before administration and discard if present. The emulsion should appear opaque and off-white to amber in color. This medication is generally well-tolerated and effective when used as directed. Always consult your healthcare provider for personalized advice and information regarding your treatment.
